title: Normalized coherent scalar quotient realization on an arbitrary scheme
statement: Fix a prime ell, finite extensions E,L of Q_ell and an embedding i:E -> L. For every scheme X, every whole-system derived reduction calculus S for E on X [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and every K-injective-normalized Roos model rho for L on X, there exists an IntegralComparisonScalarModel for i,X,S,rho [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Its natural realization identifies completed scalar extension with whole-system scalar change of S.reduction followed by total derived limit, and has the specified balanced tensor-generator normalization on every whole-system adjunction-coherent quotient presentation of each flat-term K-flat representative. No invertibility hypothesis on ell on X, constructibility, completeness or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed. Site and coefficient universes are independent. This states a single-scheme primitive scalar comparison only, without pullback data, effectivity, simultaneous choices or coherence laws.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 0941, derived extension/restriction and lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; strict scalar quotient construction in the common-stage transport argument.

proof.text: Take an ordinary quotient model and compatible derived model for S. Whole-system adjunction coherence identifies each presentation with this canonical quotient model by a strict isomorphism before total limit.

Balanced finite quotient tensor association gives the strict scalar representative and its actual quotient transitions. On generators the association sends (x tensor a) tensor b to x tensor i(a)b. Its inverse inserts the tensor unit. Applying the normalized Roos comparison identifies the scalar realization with the defining completed scalar tower.

Descend this isomorphism through the localization of flat-term K-flat representatives. For an arbitrary coherent presentation transport the strict tensor map along its canonical comparison, then use naturality of the derived change-of-rings counit and Roos comparison. This gives the displayed normalization in the entire derived system; finite evaluation is never assumed faithful.
